## Caption (verbatim)

```
The desert wasn't where God forgot about Jesus. It was where He sent Him on purpose.
Before the miracles. Before the crowds. Before a single word of His ministry was spoken — the Spirit led Him into the wilderness. Not around it. Through it.
40 days. No food. No comfort. No one cheering Him on.
And that's the part we skip over. We love the feeding of the five thousand. We love the walking on water. But we don't talk enough about the Christ who sat alone in the dust, starving, while the enemy whispered in His ear.
Here's what that tells you about your own desert season:
It doesn't mean God left. It means He's building something in you that comfort never could. The wilderness strips away everything that isn't real — your crutches, your distractions, your illusions of control. And what's left? Just you and the Father. That's exactly where He wants you.
Jesus didn't leave the desert weaker. He came out in the power of the Spirit. Every temptation He resisted became fuel for what came next. Every silent night of surrender became the foundation for every miracle the world would witness.
Your Lent doesn't need to be dramatic. It needs to be honest. One prayer at a time. One "no" to the thing that pulls you away. One morning where you choose the quiet over the noise.
The desert has always been the training ground. And God only sends His strongest there.
"Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil. And after fasting forty days and forty nights, he was hungry."
—Matthew 4:1-2
```
